content.prompt: Use Pythagoras’ theorem to find the unknown lengths in the figures below and then calculate their surface areas.

spec.description: Tall triangular prism with right angle at front bottom-right, depth up-right and three dashed hidden edges. Ordinary source colours replaced by black.
spec.mathematics: Right-triangle legs 9 cm and 40 cm, hypotenuse h cm; prism length 12 cm.

answer.short:
$h=41\text{ cm}$; surface area $1440\text{ cm}^2$.

Use Pythagoras for $h$, then add the two triangular ends and three rectangular faces.

spec.description: Triangular prism with perpendicular red dashed cross-section altitude, external base-segment arrows, right-angle mark, rear sloping labels a and b and dashed hidden rear base.
spec.mathematics: Altitude 16 mm divides base into 30 mm and 12 mm; prism length 10 mm. Unknown side lengths correspond to rear triangle slopes.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknown a and b remain unsolved.

answer.short:
$a=34\text{ mm}$, $b=20\text{ mm}$; surface area $1632\text{ mm}^2$.

Use the two right triangles to find the slopes, then add all five face areas.
